dedupe_keys.name: cardinal multiphysics coupling of nekrs and openmc in moose for fission and fusion systems

description: Cardinal is open-source software for high-fidelity multiscale and multiphysics simulation of fission and fusion energy systems. It is developed by Argonne National Laboratory and Idaho National Laboratory, which hold the copyright, with many contributors listed on the Zenodo release. It wraps the spectral element CFD code NekRS and the Monte Carlo radiation transport code OpenMC within the MOOSE framework, so that neutronics, heat transfer and fluid flow can be coupled in large simulations. The method is location-independent. Source code is on GitHub with documentation covering compilation, shell settings for many HPC systems, source documentation and tutorials, and version 0.1, tied to NekRS version 23, is archived on Zenodo (July 2026). It is licensed under the GNU Lesser General Public License 2.1 at no cost. Caveats: it needs compilation with its dependencies and high-performance computing for large problems. Simulation uses are detailed reactor core and component simulation for design and digital twins of nuclear plants. Related records: none linked on the provider's pages read on the day.
